card: This PR adds stream output operator<< overloads for commonly tested Bitcoin types in test utilities and converts bare BOOST_CHECK assertions across unit test suites to BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL and BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL_COLLECTIONS. Previously, assertion failures on custom types only reported a boolean failure without showing the mismatched values, complicating test debugging. The added display logic also prepares types for the proposed test runner overhaul in PR 35713.
changed_since_previous: Updated and expanded the callsite migrations across more unit test files, increasing the scope from 15 to 19 files.
evidence: "If the `<<` operator exists, boost can use this as a debug output when a check fails (besides `BOOST_CHECK`). This adds `<<` for types commonly used across the unit tests that do not yet have a display output." (PR description)
"All of these display strings would be used as part of #35713, but we can also use them with boost today." (PR description)
problem: When unit test assertions using `BOOST_CHECK(a == b)` fail, Boost only reports a boolean failure without printing the values of the objects being compared. Many custom Bitcoin Core types lacked stream insertion operators, preventing the use of value-printing test macros.

risk.why: Changes are strictly confined to unit test code and test utilities, meaning bugs can only cause test compilation or failure diagnostics issues.

scope_notes: A mechanical conversion of test assertions across 17 test files accompanying the new stream operator overloads in test utilities.
summary: Adds stream output `operator<<` overloads for commonly used Bitcoin types in a new test utility module (`src/test/util/common.{h,cpp}`) and updates assertion macros across unit test files. Equality checks previously using bare `BOOST_CHECK` are migrated to `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL`, `BOOST_CHECK_NE`, and `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL_COLLECTIONS` so failure diagnostics display mismatched values.
